newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Promet details Westmont buy financing.
newsitem.headline: Promet details Westmont buy financing.

text.p: Promet Bhd said on Monday that funding for the acquisition of a controlling stake in Westmont Industries Bhd would come from sources including the sale of land and property.
Other sources for financing the previously announced deal to buy 32.9 percent of Westmont are cash reserves, a small cash call and bank borrowings, Promet told a news conference.

"You will be seeing the divestment of non-core activities (within the property development business)," said Soh Chee Wen, chief executive officer and president of the maritime and construction concern.
"You'll see most of the properties being hived off within a month," he told reporters. When asked how much this would raise, he said it would be more than 100 million ringgit.

The deal with Westmont is part of a group restructuring which will see Promet's maritime engineering activities injected into Westmont. "Shipbuilding and fabrication will be rationalised under Westmont," he said.
Westmont's principal industries include engineering, construction and the servicing and repair of ships.

Related to the proposed Westmont stake acquisition, Promet said it would sell four parcels of land in the southern state of Johor. Soh said that sale plus the divestment of a fabrication yard would raise a total of 300 million ringgit.

He also said that the company will be using some of its cash reserves and make limited bank borrowings. It may also raise a small cash call, which would not be like a one-for-one rights issue, which he termed as too large.
Soh did not offer specifics on the cash call size.
Promet said that shipbuilding and oil rig fabrication would form the majority of profits over the next two years. However, the infrastructure side is catching up, he said.

Soh said that within the next three to five years, a third of group earnings would come from infrastructure and another third from shipbuilding and oil rig fabrication, with the remainder from construction and investments.
He said this was being done to avoid cyclical damage if any one sector is hit by, say, a war.

Currently, 80 percent of the group's earnings come from property-related businesses, including collection of rent and property development. The balance of profit contribution comes from maritime activities.
In its latest results for the period ended June 30, 1996, Promet posted a six-month net loss of 1.96 million ringgit or 37 cents a share on turnover of 69.28 million ringgit.
